welcome.first.text: Hi, I'm **ORBI**. Welcome to Mission Control Academy! Out here we never *know* where a spacecraft is — we **estimate** it from noisy measurements and a physics model. Ready to fly your first shift?

welcome.back.text: Welcome back, operator. Your console is warm and the tracking network is standing by.

onboard.loop.text: Every estimator runs the same loop: **predict** with physics, **compare** with a measurement, **correct** by an amount that depends on who you trust more.

onboard.truth.text: In guided missions you'll see the *true* orbit in teal. In challenges it's hidden until the debrief — just like real operations.

onboard.controls.text: Use **Space** to play/pause, **N** to step one node, **P** then **U** to step the predict and update phases separately.

onboard.ready.text: Pick **First Fix** to begin. I'll pop in whenever something interesting happens.

help.sensors.text: Sensors: switch each one on/off and tune its **assumed** noise $R$. The *true* noise is what the hardware really does — the filter only knows what you tell it.

help.estimator.text: Estimator: switching hands the current mean and covariance to the new filter, so you can compare them mid-flight.

help.processNoise.text: Process noise $Q$: how much the filter distrusts its own physics model. Bigger $Q$ means uncertainty grows faster between measurements.

help.maneuvers.text: Maneuvers: schedule a burn in the radial / transverse / normal (RTN) frame. Tick *known* to tell the filter; untick it to surprise it.

help.observability.text: Observability check: stacks $H\,\Phi$ for every planned measurement in a window and asks which state directions they can see. It's a *local, linearised* test.

help.playback.text: Playback speed only changes how fast you *watch*. The simulation steps are fixed, so results are identical at any speed.

tip.innovation.text: Tip: the **innovation** $\nu = z - h(\hat x^-)$ is the filter's surprise. Healthy filters have innovations that look like the noise they assumed.

tip.sigma.text: Tip: a good filter is not one with tiny $\sigma$ — it's one whose errors are the size it *claims* they are.

tip.alongtrack.text: Tip: along-track uncertainty grows fastest. A tiny velocity error becomes a large position error once it has had an orbit to accumulate.

tip.phase.text: Tip: step the **Predict** and **Update** phases separately and watch the ellipsoid inflate, then snap smaller.

rules.gnssOff.text: GNSS is off. From now on the filter is **dead reckoning**: it integrates its model forward with no corrections. Watch the uncertainty plot — $P$ grows as $\Phi P \Phi^\top + Q_d$ every step.

rules.outageStarted.text: Tracking outage! No measurements are arriving. The estimate keeps moving with the physics, and its uncertainty is now the only honest thing we have.

rules.rangeOnly.text: Range-only tracking measures **one** number per sample: distance. One range can't pin down a 3-D position. Try the observability check to see what a pass of ranges can and can't determine.

rules.rUp.text: You raised the assumed measurement noise. With a larger $R$ the gain $K = P H^\top (H P H^\top + R)^{-1}$ shrinks: the filter trusts each measurement **less**. Is that what the innovations say it should do?

rules.rDown.text: You told the filter the sensor is *more* precise than it is. Expect over-confidence: the filter chases the noise and its NIS climbs above the χ² band.

rules.nisSpike.text: Whoa — the innovations just jumped way outside their expected spread. Either the sensor glitched or the **model is wrong**. Open the innovations plot and look at *when* it started.

rules.qUp.text: More process noise tells the filter its predictions are shakier, so it leans harder on new measurements. Great for recovering from a surprise — but too much makes the estimate jittery.

rules.kfSelected.text: The linear KF never re-linearises. That's exact for linear dynamics, but two-body gravity isn't linear — watch for divergence once the true state drifts from its linearisation point.

rules.pfSelected.text: Particle filter selected: hundreds of possible spacecraft, weighted by how well each explains the data. Watch the effective sample size and the compute cost.

rules.allSensorsOff.text: Every sensor is off. Nothing about the state is observable now — the filter can only predict.

rules.gimbal.text: Pitch is near ±90° — **gimbal lock** for ZYX Euler angles. Roll and yaw become ambiguous and the Euler-rate equations blow up. Real flight software uses quaternions for exactly this reason.

rules.overconfident.text: The NEES says the estimate is much worse than the covariance claims. The filter is **over-confident** — a dangerous state for operations.

rules.rankDeficient.text: Rank-deficient! Some combination of states produces **no change** in any measurement you've planned. No estimator, however clever, can recover those directions from this data.

rules.unknownBurnScheduled.text: An unannounced burn is scheduled. The filter won't know — let's see if you can spot it in the residuals.

rules.knownBurnScheduled.text: Burn scheduled and the filter has been told. Its prediction will include the commanded Δv plus an execution uncertainty.

rules.truthHidden.text: Truth is hidden for this challenge. You'll have to judge the filter by its innovations alone — the debrief will reveal how you did.

lesson.complete.text: Mission complete! Let's look at the debrief.

lesson.predictionNeeded.text: Before we run: make a prediction. Committing to a guess is how you find out what you really believe.
